title: Common finite extension of finitely many complete traits
statement: Let $W_0$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K_0$ and residue field $k_0$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-field]. Let $I$ be a finite set. For each $i\in I$, let $W_i$ be a complete discrete valuation ring equipped with an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow W_i$ and finite fraction-field extension $\operatorname{Frac}(W_i)/K_0$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there exists a complete discrete valuation ring $W$ with an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow W$ making $W$ finite as a $W_0$-module and, for every $i$, a local $W_0$-map $W_i\hookrightarrow W$. The residue field $W/\mathfrak m_W$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a finite extension of $k_0$; if $k_0$ is perfect, so is this residue field.

source.place: Expose IV §4.2.3, sentence beginning De tels idéaux p étant en nombre fini: choose one finite base change dominating the finitely many Epp extensions
